react_result.final_narrative_text: Four complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on a single biological axis: perturbations to steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism. RaMP multi-DB ORA identified three WikiPathways entries at the top of its ranking — 'Steroid biosynthesis' (WP:WP496, FDR=1.01×10⁻¹⁵), 'Androgen receptor network in prostate cancer' (WP:WP2263, FDR=1.01×10⁻¹⁵), and 'Male steroid hormones in cardiomyocyte energy metabolism' (WP:WP5320, FDR=7.30×10⁻¹⁵) — with five shared driver metabolites (dihydrotestosterone, androstenedione, estrone, testosterone, dehydroepiandrosterone) simultaneously enriched. The same five steroids also drove 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' in SMPDB (SMP00068, FDR=2.95×10⁻¹⁴) and KEGG (KEGG:map00150, FDR=2.95×10⁻¹⁴), while Reactome's 'Metabolism of steroid hormones' (REACT:R-HSA-196071, FDR=1.84×10⁻¹³) captured an expanded seven-metabolite roster. Mummichog's m/z-direct network analysis independently confirmed this axis by mapping all 13 resolved query metabolites onto 'C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism' (MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism, p=1.68×10⁻⁴, overlap=13/13) as the top-ranked pathway, with 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' (MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism, p=4.20×10⁻⁴) as the second. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently validated the hsa00140 steroid hormone pathway with the same five steroids. Coumarin, spironolactone, 3-hydroxy-L-proline, pyrocatechol, and doxycycline did not participate in the steroid cluster; coumarin was instead flagged in Mummichog as a xenobiotic-metabolism singleton (p=0.040). Reconciliation confirmed zero InChIKey structural conflicts among the five driver steroids, validating that the signal is not a namespace artefact. The convergent multi-paradigm signal across ORA (RaMP/MetaboAnalystR), network (Mummichog), and graph-context (Reactome) methods strongly implicates systemic disruption of the androgen–estrogen steroid axis, likely at the level of C21-steroid biosynthesis and inter-hormone conversion reactions.

RaMP multi-DB ORA identified six top-ranked pathways sharing the same five steroids: Steroid biosynthesis (WP:WP496) at rank 1 with FDR=1.01×10⁻¹⁵, Androgen receptor network in prostate cancer (WP:WP2263) at rank 2 with FDR=1.01×10⁻¹⁵, Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00068) at rank 5 with FDR=2.95×10⁻¹⁴, Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism (KEGG:map00150) at rank 6 with FDR=2.95×10⁻¹⁴, Metabolism of steroid hormones (REACT:R-HSA-196071) at rank 8 with FDR=1.84×10⁻¹³, and Sulfatase and aromatase pathway (WP:WP5368) at rank 9 with FDR=3.07×10⁻¹². Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently ranked Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism (MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism) as the top pathway with p=0.000336 and 12 overlapping metabolites, with C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism (MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism) as rank 2 with the same p-value and 13 overlapping metabolites. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA returned hsa00140 with the same five steroids as metabolites_hit. The five driver steroids are dehydroepiandrosterone (KEGG:C01227), testosterone (KEGG:C00535), androstenedione (KEGG:C00280), estrone (KEGG:C00468), and 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one (dihydrotestosterone, KEGG:C03917). The remaining metabolites—coumarin, spironolactone, 3-hydroxy-L-proline, pyrocatechol, and doxycycline—did not map to the steroid cluster, and coumarin appeared only in the Mummichog Xenobiotics metabolism pathway at p=0.037.

  "narrative_text": "Four complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on a single biological axis: perturbations to steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism. RaMP multi-DB ORA identified three WikiPathways entries at the top of its ranking — 'Steroid biosynthesis' (WP:WP496, FDR=1.01×10⁻¹⁵), 'Androgen receptor network in prostate cancer' (WP:WP2263, FDR=1.01×10⁻¹⁵), and 'Male steroid hormones in cardiomyocyte energy metabolism' (WP:WP5320, FDR=7.30×10⁻¹⁵) — with five shared driver metabolites (dihydrotestosterone, androstenedione, estrone, testosterone, dehydroepiandrosterone) simultaneously enriched. The same five steroids also drove 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' in SMPDB (SMP00068, FDR=2.95×10⁻¹⁴) and KEGG (KEGG:map00150, FDR=2.95×10⁻¹⁴), while Reactome's 'Metabolism of steroid hormones' (REACT:R-HSA-196071, FDR=1.84×10⁻¹³) captured an expanded seven-metabolite roster. Mummichog's m/z-direct network analysis independently confirmed this axis by mapping all 13 resolved query metabolites onto 'C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism' (MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism, p=1.68×10⁻⁴, overlap=13/13) as the top-ranked pathway, with 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' (MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism, p=4.20×10⁻⁴) as the second. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently validated the hsa00140 steroid hormone pathway with the same five steroids. final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Four complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on a single biological axis: perturbations to steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism. RaMP multi-DB ORA identified three WikiPathways entries at the top of its ranking — 'Steroid biosynthesis' (WP:WP496, FDR=1.01×10⁻¹⁵), 'Androgen receptor network in prostate cancer' (WP:WP2263, FDR=1.01×10⁻¹⁵), and 'Male steroid hormones in cardiomyocyte energy metabolism' (WP:WP5320, FDR=7.30×10⁻¹⁵) — with five shared driver metabolites (dihydrotestosterone, androstenedione, estrone, testosterone, dehydroepiandrosterone) simultaneously enriched. The same five steroids also drove 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' in SMPDB (SMP00068, FDR=2.95×10⁻¹⁴) and KEGG (KEGG:map00150, FDR=2.95×10⁻¹⁴), while Reactome's 'Metabolism of steroid hormones' (REACT:R-HSA-196071, FDR=1.84×10⁻¹³) captured an expanded seven-metabolite roster. Mummichog's m/z-direct network analysis independently confirmed this axis by mapping all 13 resolved query metabolites onto 'C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism' (MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism, p=1.68×10⁻⁴, overlap=13/13) as the top-ranked pathway, with 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' (MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism, p=4.20×10⁻⁴) as the second. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently validated the hsa00140 steroid hormone pathway with the same five steroids. Coumarin, spironolactone, 3-hydroxy-L-proline, pyrocatechol, and doxycycline did not participate in the steroid cluster; coumarin was instead flagged in Mummichog as a xenobiotic-metabolism singleton (p=0.040). Reconciliation confirmed zero InChIKey structural conflicts among the five driver steroids, validating that the signal is not a namespace artefact. The convergent multi-paradigm signal across ORA (RaMP/MetaboAnalystR), network (Mummichog), and graph-context (Reactome) methods strongly implicates systemic disruption of the androgen–estrogen steroid axis, likely at the level of C21-steroid biosynthesis and inter-hormone conversion reactions.
